articles.title: From Zombie Fungi to Toothless Birds: How David Attenborough's Legacy Lives on in Species Names
articles.summary: Over 50 organisms bear David Attenborough's name, honoring the naturalist who inspired generations of scientists. A fungus that controls cave spiders, a 120-million-year-old toothless bird, and a rainbow worm are among the tributes marking his 100th birthday.

articles.title: Sound-Activated Nanoparticles Could Bring Light Therapy Deep into the Body—No Incisions Needed
articles.summary: Stanford researchers have developed mechanoluminescent nanoparticles that emit light when triggered by ultrasound, enabling deep-tissue illumination in mice. The breakthrough could revolutionize gene editing, cancer therapy, and optogenetics without invasive procedures.

articles.title: A Nobel Economist's Reality Check on AI and Jobs: Agents, Influence, and the Usability Gap
articles.summary: Daron Acemoglu, a Nobel laureate in economics, remains skeptical about an AI jobs apocalypse. He points to AI agents' struggle with task-switching, the risk of biased research from tech-hired economists, and the lack of user-friendly AI apps as key factors limiting disruption.
